label: Widening storm
summary: The world falls to 34 as the Gulf war opens a second front at sea and Europe burns. The US completed a 13th consecutive night of strikes on Iran, killing at least four people in Khuzestan with explosions reported across six more provinces, while President Trump told Axios he was weighing a 'massive attack' bigger than anything yet and threatened to hit 'one bridge or power plant' in Tehran itself; Iran answered with drones on American bases in Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi promised 'an eye for an eye.' The sharper turn came in the Red Sea, where Houthi forces struck two Saudi tankers, the Encelia and the Layla, setting both alight in the first attack since they declared a blockade of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a chokepoint carrying roughly 12 percent of world trade; Brent leapt about 6 percent to top 100 dollars for the first time since May, up some 40 percent this month, and Wall Street sold off with the Nasdaq down 2.1 percent and the S&P 500 off 1.21 percent to 7,408.30. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told senators the war has cost 37.5 billion dollars, with 18 American dead and about 447 wounded, as the House passed a 95 billion dollar framework by 216-214. Europe's fires forced roughly 60,000 people from their homes in France, 40,000 on the Cap-Ferret peninsula alone, while Spain declared a national emergency with nearly 20,000 evacuated near Madrid. Monsoon floods killed at least 82 across northeastern India, Pakistan and Afghanistan; Chile buried 10 dead from flooding; and DR Congo's Ebola outbreak reached 2,473 cases and about 1,000 deaths with four in five new cases untraceable. The lighter column was thin but real: South Korea replaced 'denuclearisation first' with a 'peace first' opening to Pyongyang, 27 nations met at the ASEAN Regional Forum in Manila where Rubio and Lavrov held a rare bilateral, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea signed a defence cooperation pact, US jobless claims fell to 187,000, the lowest since 1969, and NASA detailed an Artemis III orbital rehearsal in which Orion will dock with both the Blue Origin and SpaceX landers. The headline matches the rubric formula with no adjustment.

drivers.headline: The US bombs Iran for a 13th consecutive night, killing at least four people in Khuzestan province with explosions reported across six other provinces, as President Trump tells Axios he is 'considering a massive attack' that would be 'bigger than ever before' and is 'close to making a decision'; Iran retaliates with drone strikes on US facilities including Sheikh Isa Airbase in Bahrain, Muwaffaq Salti in Jordan and Ali Al Salem in Kuwait, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warns of 'an eye for an eye' while Secretary of State Marco Rubio answers that Trump's approach is 'a head for an eye'

Yemen's Houthis open a new maritime front by striking two Saudi oil tankers, the Encelia and the Layla, in the Red Sea, setting fires aboard both with no casualties reported; it is their first attack since declaring a blockade of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which carries roughly 12 percent of global trade, in retaliation for Saudi Arabia's blockade of Yemen and a strike on Sanaa airport, and Trump warns of 'major military punishment,' saying the US 'will hold Iran responsible, in that the Houthis are a Surrogate and/or Proxy of Iran'

Brent crude jumps about 6 percent to break 100 dollars a barrel for the first time since May, roughly 40 percent higher on the month, as the Red Sea attacks compound Iran's disruption of the Strait of Hormuz; US equities slide with the Nasdaq down 2.1 percent and briefly under 25,000, the S&P 500 off 1.21 percent to 7,408.30 and the Dow down 0.9 percent, with Alphabet and Tesla falling as raised capital-spending plans sharpen doubts about returns on AI, though initial jobless claims unexpectedly drop to 187,000, the lowest since 1969

President Zelenskyy replaces armed forces commander Oleksandr Syrsky with 43-year-old Major General Mykhailo Drapatyi, a reshuffle following nationwide protests over the dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, as the UN reports 1,396 Ukrainian civilians killed in the first half of 2026, a 37 percent rise year on year; Russian missile barrages this week killed at least ten civilians in the Donetsk and Odesa regions while Ukrainian drones struck a Russian oil refinery some 400 miles beyond the border

Wildfires drive more than 60,000 people from their homes in southern France, including 40,000 ordered off the Cap-Ferret peninsula near Bordeaux and 23,000 in the Landes, after a blaze that began at Saumos consumed 3,400 hectares of pine forest in temperatures above 30C with strengthening easterly winds; Spain declares a national emergency as nearly 20,000 evacuate villages near Madrid with about 6,000 hectares burned, and two firefighters died earlier in the week battling a fire near Bordeaux airport

At least 82 people are killed across northeastern India, Pakistan and Afghanistan as relentless rains and flash floods destroy roads, bridges and farmland and displace thousands, with wrecked infrastructure hampering relief and the monsoon still weeks from peak intensity; the same day five Thai security personnel are killed and six civilians wounded, two of them children, when insurgents strike a market during the morning rush in Thailand's southern provinces

Chile mourns 10 people killed by widespread flooding that damaged more than 23,000 homes, while Brazil absorbs the cost of protectionism as a 25 percent US tariff takes hold; the region's one clear bright spot is Argentina, whose credit risk improves after Moody's lifts its sovereign rating from Caa1 to B3, and Colombia's Congress completes an orderly election of a new Senate president

The WHO warns of unprecedented transmission in the Bundibugyo-virus Ebola outbreak in DR Congo and Uganda, reporting 2,473 infections and about 1,000 deaths since mid-May with roughly 80 percent of new cases linked to unknown transmission chains, as armed groups attack medical clinics and hamper MSF and WHO operations; Human Rights Watch separately reports Niger's junta has 'significantly tightened its grip' three years after its coup, and Madagascar documents 172 missing minors in early 2026, eight of them found dead

Juan Jairo Coronilla Durán, a Mexican tourist visiting Florida on a legitimate visa, is killed by a semi-truck near St. Augustine while fleeing immigration agents, the fourth ICE-related death in under a week; House Democrats report that of 56 complaints of excessive force filed against ICE officers only one was referred for discipline, with Representative Jamie Raskin saying more than 50 people have died in ICE custody since the administration took office

New Zealand and Papua New Guinea sign a Statement of Intent on Defence Cooperation for 2026-2029, expanding dialogue, training, joint exercises and personnel exchanges, with Defence Minister Chris Penk saying 'Pacific nations like ours are stronger when we work closely together'; the same day American Samoa secures a 493,002 dollar CDC grant to strengthen disease surveillance and Pacific ICT officials meet in Port Moresby to finalise regional recommendations on artificial intelligence and digital transformation, though the Pacific Islands Forum again fails to agree a statement on China's 6 July missile launch near Tuvalu

Seoul announces a 'peace first' engagement policy toward North Korea, replacing its long-standing 'denuclearisation first' doctrine and allowing humanitarian exchanges and family reunions without preconditions on Pyongyang's weapons programmes; at the ASEAN Regional Forum in Manila, 27 nations meet with the Gulf war and Hormuz disruption dominating talks, Secretary of State Rubio and Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov hold a rare bilateral, and Wang Yi meets Philippine counterpart Maria Theresa Lazaro to stress dialogue after a shoal incident

NASA details an unusually ambitious orbital rehearsal for Artemis III in 2027, in which Orion astronauts will separately rendezvous and dock with prototype lunar landers from Blue Origin and SpaceX in low Earth orbit, with up to two suited astronauts entering the Blue Moon test article and Starship docking nose-to-nose; three heavy rockets will launch in rapid succession over the two-week mission to reduce risk before crewed lunar landings resume in 2028
